source_refs.note: Run-in heading Multiple Inheritance under Inheritance, with Figure 3.4 and the Father/Mother/Child example (PDF 41-42, printed 37-38).

blocks.text: Multiple inheritance in Python allows a single class to inherit features (attributes and methods) from more than one parent class. This enables a child class to combine behaviors from different sources, such as a Smartphone class inheriting from both a Camera and a Computer class (as shown in Figure 3.4).

blocks.alt: Multiple inheritance: a Child Class box below two boxes, Parent Class 1 and Parent Class 2; lines from the child go to both parents, each ending in a hollow arrowhead at the parent.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.4: Multiple Inheritance (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.4).

blocks.text: In this example, the Child class inherits from both Father and Mother classes. It can access methods from both parent classes.
